classification.difficultyReason: Substitute a supplied ordered pair into two linear equations and decide whether both hold.

questions.mappingNote: Part a verifies two true equalities. Part b distinguishes satisfying the second equation from satisfying both equations. Both directly assess verification by substitution rather than graphical or algebraic solution.
questions.methodNote: The introduction identifies a simultaneous solution as a point satisfying both equations. Example 1's continuation and Example 2 check both equations by substituting the proposed coordinates.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Substitute a supplied ordered pair into two linear equations and decide whether both hold.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct three familiar line graphs on common axes, read the specified pairwise intersections and verify by direct substitution; the requested graphical method and pair selection are explicit.

questions.mappingNote: Part a constructs three lines on common axes. Parts b(i–iii) read each specified pair's intersection. Graphical simultaneous equations is the directly assessed skill; substitution supports the taught checks.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 plots two points on each line, optionally checks a third, reads the intersection and checks it by substitution. Example 2 also demonstrates plotting by intercepts.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct three familiar line graphs on common axes, read the specified pairwise intersections and verify by direct substitution; the requested graphical method and pair selection are explicit.

classification.difficultyReason: Repeatedly construct two graphs from given equations, read their intersection and check both equations; exact fractions are absent but some plots require extending the displayed integer-point construction.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly assesses graphical simultaneous equations followed by substitution checks; no algebraic solution method replaces the requested graphs.
questions.methodNote: Example 1 plots two points for each line and reads their intersection. Example 2 uses intercepts. Both require checking the intersection by substitution into both original equations.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Repeatedly construct two graphs from given equations, read their intersection and check both equations; exact fractions are absent but some plots require extending the displayed integer-point construction.

classification.difficultyReason: Draw two specified familiar straight lines and connect their common gradient/different intercepts to the explicitly requested no-solution interpretation.

questions.mappingNote: Question 4 extends the graphical intersection method to two distinct parallel lines; the absence of an intersection means no solution.
questions.methodNote: Plot two points for each straight line on common axes and interpret common points as simultaneous solutions.

classification.difficultyReason: Draw coincident lines and interpret their common points as infinitely many solutions.

questions.methodNote: A simultaneous solution is a point lying on both graphs; the worked examples identify solutions from intersections.
